newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks close firmer, market to stay busy.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks close firmer, market to stay busy.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mostly firmer on Tuesday, led by blue chips, and traders said the market could stay busy this week.
"For now, there is still interest...where there is profit, you are bound to have investors who will be eager to buy or sell," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage.

Nenad Pavletic, trader at Auctor brokerage, said "the summer season does not mean there will be no trading. There might be a small correction in prices, but it does not mean the volume of trade will fall drastically."
Ten of the 18 active issues rose, four fell, three were flat and one traded for the first time. Volume more than doubled to 37,035 shares, turnover also rose to 28.7 million kuna.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka traded heavily, and traders said their share prices in Zagreb would track their Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) in London.
Zagrebacka climbed 49 kuna to 2,160 on volume of 3,751 shares. Its GDRs were stronger at $34.3 in the afternoon, up from $33.625 at the opening.
Its bearer stock closed 20 kuna higher at 870, while its preference shares added 10 kuna to 1,500.

The most active stock was shipyard Viktor Lenac, which last week joined Zagrebacka, Pliva and Varazdinska Banka in the top segment of the central bourse. It sold 15,563 shares, inching up one kuna to 156.
Dubrovacka Banka I-series made its market debut, selling 1,662 units at 7,000 kuna each. Brokers expected the bank's shares to rise amid higher volumes.
"It is rather strange Dubrovacka has not been active before since it is a good bank. It is ranked among Croatia's six top banks according to profit," Pavletic said.
Top gainer hotelier Istraturist added 10 kuna, or 6.3 percent, to 170 kuna on volume of 741 shares. Biggest decliner Dalmatinska Banka lost 29 kuna, or 9.1 percent, to 309 kuna with 105 shares sold.
Food processor Podravka shed three kuna to 242, with 5,051 units changing hands. Nikolac did not expect the stock to fall further.
Brewery Karlovacka pivovara added 20 kuna to 530, with 1,526 shares traded.
